items.topic: Generated vs custom files in a JUDO project
items.claim: No documentation tells how to separate generator output from developer-written code in a JUDO project.
items.fact: Use the generator's own conventions, not file headers: `.gitignore` blocks (`# JUDO GENERATOR BLOCK START`), `.generator-ignore`, and `*.default` siblings. In a fresh clone generated code is gitignored, so a tracked file under a generator-owned folder is custom. Custom: model/*.model, src/custom/** (frontend), generator-overrides/** (.hbs templates), *CustomImplementation.java, OperationCallInterceptor/WriteGuard, hand-written modules (common, report, scheduler...). Generated but committed on purpose: schema migrations, some .default files. Measured on rackinspect 3954ae1.

items.topic: G E N E R A T E D header does not mean untouched
items.claim: Files with the 'G E N E R A T E D' header are generated and untouched.
items.fact: 57 of 192 tracked *CustomImplementation.java still carry the stub 'G E N E R A T E D' header but are fully implemented. The *.java.default stubs (245) just throw UnsupportedOperationException; 53 model operations have only the stub (no implementation). Compare against the .default sibling instead of the header.

items.topic: Custom operation implementations map to model operations via interface path
items.fact: Each ...CustomImplementation.java implements an interface `...operation.<model>.<path>.<Op>`; that path names the model operation. Interceptors (66 OperationCallInterceptor, 11 WriteGuard with allowed roles + operations() list) map to operations via operations() lists. Frontend: 856 generated customization.ts files declare hook interfaces; application-customizer.tsx in src/custom registers ~370 hooks.

Schema migrations are 18 steps (diff model + Liquibase changesets 00..08); only non-empty data-migration changesets (04, 06) carry developer knowledge. judo.sh commands: env|clean|prune|update|generate|generate-root|dump|import|build|reckless|start|stop|status|schema-upgrade; generate uses `-DgenerateApplication -DskipApplicationBuild`, generate-root `-DgenerateRoot`.

items.topic: Sweep driven by subagents, not flows
items.fact: Operator rejected the pi-flows sweep: 'ok don't do it using flows spawn subagents so we can control it better'. Sweep driven from operator's session via references/sweep.md; scripts for deterministic steps; subagents judo-sweep-explore-*(model/backend/frontend/schema, read-only), cross-validate (operator approves decisions.json), author (writes only catalog/** and fragments/**), max 3 gate fix rounds, operator confirms before push. Subagents use model roles `@<role>`.

items.topic: A/B testing and reconstruction deferred / not part of sweep
items.fact: 'for A/B for now none! later we can do this! for Reconstruction also defer it'; then: 'no reconstruction or A/B testing you will just explore and update the blueprints, best practices, models and agent docs from models and the judo-ng (that is domain knowledge)'.

items.topic: Agent-docs first, kb-ify, review all judo-ng explorer findings
items.fact: 'you do the agent-docs first also kb-ify it as well! FIRST the agent-docs KEEP IN MIND! review everything the explore agents will bring up from judo-ng code!' Agent-docs update has priority over blueprint/best-practice sweep, and must conform to kb format.

items.topic: Skill must not contain domain knowledge
items.fact: 'The skill must not contain the domain knowledge update! That is not needed later as much as the blueprint and best practices update!' Domain knowledge update is not a skill responsibility; prioritise blueprint and best-practices updates.

items.claim: A flow could fan out one explorer per project.
items.fact: pi-flows 0.9.0 (installed, npm latest, source repo develop 6fc77df) has 5 step types (agent, fork, agent-decision, code, code-decision); no dynamic fan-out (`map` step proposed in openspec/changes/map-step, 0/10 tasks), no `when:` guard (node-when-guard), no built-in worktrees (only via code handlers), no sandbox (agent-docker-sandbox unreleased).

items.topic: kb guard: consult kb before repeated source searching
items.fact: The kb guard emits '[kb] Repeated source searching, still no kb consult' after repeated grep/find; run kb_search / kb agents <path> / kb get first. Also reads without offset/limit and large outputs are replaced by ctx stubs.

items.claim: Template ships agent-docs (74 files: backend 12, deployment 7, domain 4, e2e-testing 7, frontend 16, integration-testing 8, model 19, README.md.hbs).
items.fact: Commit 5bddd8b 'JNG-6380 Remove agent-docs from the template' (branch feature/JNG-6380_cli_guidance, already contained in origin/develop; develop has 0 agent-docs files). Template's JUDOSPEC agent system (18 subagents, 10 commands, 32 hooks) is extracted via openspec change extract-agent-tooling-from-template; judo-blueprint now holds the agent-docs; a new pi plugin takes agent behaviour. Generated AGENTS.md/openspec/project.md/agent-docs are checksum-tracked and overwritten by ./judo.sh generate-root (release notes say so); generateAgentCli name kept.

items.topic: judo-ng repos carrying their own agent-docs
items.fact: judo-ng/runtime/judo-runtime-core/* modules (accessmanager, security, dao-rdbms, dao-rdbms-liquibase, dao-rdbms-hsqldb, expression, guice-*, spring-*) have their own agent-docs/ dirs (73 md files total) — source for domain knowledge. Blueprint repo catalog: best-practices frontend 62, backend 74, model 71; agent-docs frontend 16, backend 12, integration-testing 6, e2e-testing 7, deployment 7, model 15, domain 1. judo-ng top-level: models (judo-meta-*), packages, spring, template, runtime.
